  • A comprehensive new review published on November 5 in the journal Science evaluated the current evidence on how GLP-1 medications like semaglutide and tirzepatide may affect the brain across aging, cardiometabolic disease, and Alzheimer’s disease.
  • In a recent development, the authors of the review suggested that GLP-1 medications like Ozempic and Zepbound may offer brain health benefits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GLP-1 medications have transformed obesity and type 2 diabetes treatment. Now, researchers are investigating whether the effects of this blockbuster class of drugs extend beyond weight loss and affect brain health.

A comprehensive new review published on November 5 in the journal Science evaluated the current evidence on how GLP-1 medications like semaglutide and tirzepatide may affect the brain across aging, cardiometabolic disease, and Alzheimer’s disease.

In a recent development, the authors of the review suggested that GLP-1 medications like Ozempic and Zepbound may offer brain health benefits. However, they were also left with the question of whether the medications act directly on the brain or whether better brain health is actually a consequence of improved cardiometabolic health.

Sheena Aurora, MD, vice president, Medical Affairs, Alzheimer’s Association, who wasn’t involved in the review, told Healthline that more research is needed to better understand the effects of GLP-1 drugs on the brain.

“While research suggests GLP-1s could reduce brain inflammation, improve blood vessel health, and even protect neurons, much broader, randomized clinical trials on GLP-1s and brain health, including in people with Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias, are needed,” she said.

It has been revealed that GLP-1 medications like semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, mimic the GLP-1 hormone. Tirzepatide, the active ingredient in Mounjaro and Zepbound, also targets a second hormone pathway called GIP.

These medications have been shown to produce significant weight loss and improvements in cardiometabolic health.

This is important for brain health because obesity, type 2 diabetes, and vascular dysfunction are all linked with cognitive impairment and dementia. Insulin resistance and chronic inflammation may also link metabolic and brain health.

Sources indicate that analyses of large outcome trials and observational cohorts have suggested that GLP-1 medications may be associated with a reduced risk of cognitive impairment and dementia. However, randomized trials in diseases like Alzheimer’s disease have yet to demonstrate clinical benefits.

Around 200 preclinical and mechanistic studies have shown benefits for learning, memory, synaptic plasticity, and neuronal resilience, though results are heterogeneous in design and direction, so a clear consensus on magnitude and mechanism remains lacking.

Sources indicate that it is also unclear how well GLP-1 medications reach the brain. They appear to reach certain areas, such as the hypothalamus, brainstem, and circumventricular organs, more readily than regions protected by the blood-brain barrier.

Industry observers note that the report authors noted that some studies have shown that GLP-1 receptor agonists may reduce the risk of cognitive impairment and dementia in people with type 2 diabetes. This may be due to cognitive challenges being linked to factors such as blood sugar, blood pressure, vascular health, and sleep.

Mir Ali, MD, medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center in Fountain Valley, CA, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline, “These findings are interesting, but like many of the other benefits associated with GLP-1 medications, a direct causal relationship has not yet been proven.”.

“Rather, the benefits appear to be more closely tied to the reduction in obesity and better control of diabetes,” he noted.

Aurora noted that growing evidence supports the heart-brain connection.

She cited newly introduced findings from the Alzheimer’s Association’s landmark U.S. POINTER study presented at the Clinical Trials in Alzheimer’s Disease (CTAD) conference November 16–19 in Boston, MA.

The research demonstrated that the structured lifestyle intervention program also improved heart health risk factors, such as:.

According to recent reports, “U.S. POINTER can change those risk factors within 24 months, and better heart health risk-factor control was linked with better cognition,” Aurora stated. “We’re also interested to see whether adding a drug like a GLP-1 to a U.S. POINTER-style lifestyle program improves cognition in at-risk older adults more than the program alone.”.

To find out, the Alzheimer’s Association is funding the Prevention of Risk for Cognitive Decline through Combined Therapy (PROTECT-Cog) global phase 3 clinical trial.

PROTECT-Cog is a first-of-its-kind trial designed to evaluate whether combining a proven multidomain lifestyle intervention with a metabolism-targeting drug, like a GLP-1, can further reduce the risk of cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment, and dementia in at-risk older adults.

Dung Trinh, MD, internist at MemorialCare Medical Group and Chief Medical Officer of Healthy Brain Clinic in Irvine, CA, who also wasn’t involved in the review, told Healthline, “I often remind my patients that what’s good for the heart is generally good for the brain.”.

Sources indicate that “The brain depends on a healthy cardiovascular system to deliver a constant supply of oxygen, glucose, and other nutrients. Conditions such as high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, and high cholesterol can damage blood vessels, promote chronic inflammation, and increase the risk of stroke and vascular cognitive impairment,” he remarked.

“Over time, these changes can also contribute to the development or progression of dementia.”.

Trinh added that while GLP-1 medications can improve several cardiometabolic risk factors, these improvements do not automatically translate into proven dementia prevention.

“Regular physical activity, a heart-healthy diet, adequate sleep, and management of cardiovascular risk factors remain essential strategies for maintaining brain health as we age,” he said.

When the report authors turned their attention to more stringent tests on semaglutide in people already living with early Alzheimer’s disease, the picture began to change.

Novo Nordisk’s EVOKE and EVOKE + Phase 3 Trials examined the efficacy of semaglutide in people with early stage Alzheimer’s disease.

The studies revealed that while semaglutide produced changes in several disease-related biomarkers, it didn’t slow the progression of Alzheimer’s disease.

Recent findings suggest that this emphasizes that fixing metabolic problems might prevent cognitive decline in someone with obesity or diabetes. But it might not be enough to reverse the damage in someone with established Alzheimer’s disease, where profound synaptic loss and protein pathology have already occurred.

The review authors suggest that future research on obesity and diabetes should also include rigorous and specific cognitive testing.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The invention’s speed comes from a novel compound steam engine that allows highly pressurized air to expand throughout numerous chambers not once but twice.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in 2022, researchers at the University of California San Diego developed a 3D-printed soft robot that used air power to scuttle along at a modest 1.5 inches per second. After a few years of adjustments, the engineering team now has a six-legged iteration that leaves its predecessor in the dust. Detailed in a study published in the journal Science Robotics, their newly introduced soft robot still contains no electronics, but runs across multiple types of terrain at speeds topping 15 feet per second. According to its designers, the machine is the fastest soft robot ever constructed.

In a recent development, “Our first walking robot demonstrated what was possible, but it was too slow. We hoped to overcome this limitation, and we were fortunate to find a solution to make the new robot 100 times faster,” Yichen Zhai, a study co-author and UC San Diego engineer, noted in a statement.

The invention’s speed comes from a novel compound steam engine that allows highly pressurized air to expand throughout numerous chambers not once but twice. This air first flows through the robot’s valves, then recirculates through wider, lower-pressure sections in its legs. The team’s creation maintained its efficiency and speed in multiple environments, including gravel, grass, mulch, and concrete. It even handles sandy surfaces and can work underwater.

“The key challenge was to implement a time-tested solution (the compound steam engine) in a soft running robot that can be printed in a single piece out of a single material,” explained Zhai. “We see this as a step towards complex and powerful robots that can be printed on the desktop using inexpensive materials.”.

Their current version of the robot is still limited by its power source, and the tethered hose that delivers the pressurized. That noted, they blueprint to design future variants requiring less air. This would hypothetically allow them to attach a portable power source like a compressed air cartridge, as well as enable more complex controls and maneuvering.

These prototypes are more than oddball experiments, too. Without any onboard electronics, similar robots could have an advantage while operating in highly irradiated environments, dangerous conditions, and even outer space.

According to recent reports, A newly introduced EQS 500 4Matic version makes an appearance for 2027, with two electric motors making 469 horsepower. The base EQS 450+, which is rear-wheel drive, now makes 402 hp, up 47 hp compared to last year’s model. The top-spec EQS 580 4Matic, meanwhile, gets a 40-hp increase for a total of 576 hp.

It has been revealed that the 2027 EQS Sedan comes standard with Mercedes’ Airmatic air suspension with Intelligent Damper Control, as well as the company’s next-generation Digital Light system with Adaptive Highbeam Assist Plus. A dual-plug charging port with NACS for DC fast charging and J1772 for AC charging is part of the package for American-spec models.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, the 2027 EQE SUV and 2027 EQS SUV are carryover models with minimal changes compared to the outgoing models. There are no changes to the EQE SUV, while the EQS SUV’s standard equipment now includes Anodized Aluminum Roof Rails, and the wheel selection features new designs. As previously reported, the top-spec Mercedes-Maybach EQS SUV has been discontinued for 2027.

Recent findings suggest that the 2027 Mercedes-Benz EQS Sedan starts at $101,450 for the base EQS 450+, while the top EQS 580 4Matic trim starts at $123,900. The 2027 EQE SUV starts at $64,950, while the 2027 EQS SUV starts at $89,950.

Sources indicate that sales of Mercedes-Benz's EQ lineup have been lackluster, to say the least, and after the discontinuation of the EQE Sedan earlier this year, there have been voices claiming that the German automaker was prepared to retire more electric models. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that but there’s a catch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is rolling out an revision that makes the Cybertruck turn even tighter, improving on what was already one of the best turning radiuses you can get in a full-size pickup.

Recent findings suggest that but there’s a catch. It only works on 2027 model year Cybertrucks, and Tesla plans to stop building the truck by the end of next summer.

Tesla’s official Cybertruck account posted a short drone video early Saturday showing a truck doing circles in a parking lot, with a “before” and “after” comparison of its turning path. “Even tighter turns now rolling out to newly introduced Cybertrucks,” the account wrote.

In a follow-up post, Tesla said the improvement requires software version 2026.44 or newer and “only applies to model year 2027 Cybertrucks.”.

It's not the size … it's how you maneuver itEven tighter turns now rolling out to latest Cybertrucks pic.twitter.com/FuNoox4ax0.

Tesla didn’t share a latest turning circle figure. In the video, the “after” circle is visibly smaller than the “before” one by what looks to be at least a foot.

Recent findings suggest that the Cybertruck’s maneuverability comes from its rear-wheel steering paired with steer-by-wire. At low speeds, the rear wheels turn opposite to the fronts, which shrinks the space the truck needs to make a U-turn. We’ve been tracking the Cybertruck’s four-wheel steering since the prototype days, when Tesla was showing it off in parking garages.

Even before this revision, the results were impressive. Tesla’s owner’s manual lists the Cybertruck’s curb-to-curb turning circle at about 43.5 ft (13.25 m). That beats the Ford F-150 Lightning at roughly 47.8 ft and the Rivian R1T at 44.9 ft, and it’s within about 4 ft of a Model Y. Not bad for a 6,600-lb truck that’s nearly 19 feet long.

It has been revealed that and Tesla always noted there was more to come. At launch, the rear wheels turned only about 3 degrees. In early 2024, a Tesla engineer said a software update would push that to 10 degrees, and Elon Musk said the tech giant had improvements in the works to “tighten the turning circle significantly.”.

Industry observers note that tesla hasn’t said whether this patch delivers the full 10 degrees, or why it’s limited to 2027 trucks. If it comes down to hardware, owners of earlier Cybertrucks who were counting on this as an over-the-air upgrade are out of luck.

Industry observers note that credit where it’s due. The turning circle is one of the best things about the Cybertruck, and anyone who has driven one knows it. Steer-by-wire combined with rear-wheel steering is real engineering, and other vehicles are just starting to get that combo a couple years after Cybertruck had it. Making it even better is a nice update.

But it’s hard to get excited about it.

Recent findings suggest that and 39.4 feet turning circle for the Cadillac Escalade which also has rear wheel steering. As does the iX5 (39.7'), MB GLC (36.7') and EQS (35.8'), the Lucid Gravity (38.4), Hummer 37.4', Cayenne (38.4) and a around two dozen other vehicles on the market today. So maybe this is not such big news after all?

In a recent development, earlier this month, Musk announced that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas to make room for Cybercab. He has since pushed the end date to the end of summer 2027 to work through an “order backlog.” We estimate Tesla is delivering about 7,000 to 8,000 Cybertrucks a quarter, roughly 12% of the 250,000 units a year it planned for.

So Tesla is improving a 2027 model year truck that it will stop making next summer. And since Tesla now only sells the $109,990 Cyberbeast, the people getting this upgrade are the few still buying the most expensive Cybertruck in its final months. It does nothing about what actually sank the truck: pricing that never came close to the $39,900 promised in 2019, range and towing that fell short, and a design most truck buyers never warmed up to.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a cool engineering flex on a product with an expiration date. If Tesla had delivered this kind of polish on the $40,000 truck it promised, would we be writing the Cybertruck’s obituary right now?

By 2040, 51% of People Living with HIV Could Be Over 50

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Advances in antiretroviral therapy (ART) have helped people living with HIV live longer, contributing to a growing population of older adults with the virus.
  • In fact, a recent report published in The Lancet HIV projects that approximately 51% of people living with HIV worldwide will be over age 50 by 2040.
  • The report’s authors emphasized the “pressing need” for HIV prevention and screening services tailored to older adults, who face additional age-related challenges when accessing care.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Advances in antiretroviral therapy (ART) have helped people living with HIV live longer, contributing to a growing population of older adults with the virus.

In fact, a recent report published in The Lancet HIV projects that approximately 51% of people living with HIV worldwide will be over age 50 by 2040. An estimated 96% of these older adults will live in low- and middle-income countries.

The report’s authors emphasized the “pressing need” for HIV prevention and screening services tailored to older adults, who face additional age-related challenges when accessing care.

These challenges include stigma related to both age and HIV, a higher burden of chronic health conditions, taking multiple medications, delayed diagnoses, physical limitations, and increased financial and social vulnerability.

Factors like these “influence HIV risk for older adults in complex and dynamic ways,” according to the report authors.

Several factors have contributed to the growing population of older adults living with HIV, including:.

Industry observers note that many adults over age 50 who are living with HIV acquired the virus during young adulthood in the late 1990s and early 2000s. During that period, some experienced prolonged periods of uncontrolled HIV and exposure to older ART medications with more severe side effects, which may have contributed to long-term inflammation and other health complications.

William Schaffner, MD, professor in the Division of Infectious Diseases at Vanderbilt University, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline, “That older persons with HIV are on track to outnumber younger persons with HIV infection is a double-barreled success story.”.

According to recent reports, “First, the effective treatment of persons with HIV infection has resulted in the expectation of normal or near-normal lifespans; thus, more older persons living with HIV infection,” he said. “This is a great success; both in creating effective, easy-to-use medicines as well as developing medical care systems that can reach such patients and provide lifetime care.”.

Schaffner mentioned the second success has been educating younger people about HIV prevention, helping reduce new infections.

Older adults also account for a growing proportion of newly introduced HIV diagnoses. They are more likely to receive a diagnosis later in the course of infection, which can delay treatment and increase the risk of serious health complications and death.

Mathematical models project that the average age of people living with HIV worldwide will increase from 41 in 2025 to 50 by 2040, largely driven by demographic shifts in low- and middle-income countries.

It has been revealed that while the World Health Organization (WHO) does not specify an upper age limit for HIV testing in its published overview, U.S. guidelines focus on specific age groups.

Sources indicate that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends routine HIV testing for people ages 13 to 64, and the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force recommends testing for people ages 15 to 65.

In a recent development, however, these age limits don’t mean older adults shouldn’t be tested for HIV, as both U.S. organizations also recommend testing older adults who may be at risk.

According to recent reports, older adults can still be sexually active and have a chance of acquiring HIV. Certain physical changes that come with age, such as thinning of vaginal tissue, may also increase the risk of HIV infection.

Despite these risks, older adults are often overlooked in HIV prevention campaigns, research, and clinical trials. The report’s authors say more needs to be done to address these gaps.

“Targeted and tailored HIV prevention and screening services for older adults are a pressing global need,” the report authors stated.

Schaffner agreed with this and added, “Increasing the effectiveness of diagnosis and treatment of HIV infection in older adults will increase their expectation of a healthier, longer life.”.

The report recommends several approaches to improving HIV prevention and screening among older adults, including:.

While Schaffner noted that HIV treatment has “advanced spectacularly over the past 20 years,” making it possible for people living with HIV to lead longer, healthier lives, access to these treatments remains a challenge in many parts of the world.

  • “His family was all on board with it,” current wing commander and retired pilot Rob Jenner told St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More than 85 years have passed since the very first B-25 bombers rolled off the assembly line. The legendary, twin-engine aircraft flew above every theater of World War II, and were instrumental to the Allied forces’ victory. Many B-25 bombers are preserved in museums, but a handful of them actually remain flightworthy today.

Sources indicate that one of those flight-ready B25s is a plane nicknamed Show Me. The aircraft belongs to the Missouri Wing of the Commemorative Air Force, and has taken to the sky every fall since 2009 to demonstrate its impressive aerial bombardment capabilities. But Show Me doesn’t unleash an arsenal of destruction anymore. Instead, the B25 releases a bevy of hollowed-out pumpkins filled with red, white, and blue pool chalk. However, aircraft recently dropped more than gourds for onlookers outside St. Louis. During this year’s flight, Show Me also deployed a pumpkin stuffed with the ashes of the Missouri Wing’s late, beloved volunteer, Lou Tacchi, Jr.

“His family was all on board with it,” current wing commander and retired pilot Rob Jenner told St. Louis public radio. “They had shirts printed up, and they called it the ‘Pop Drop.’”.

Industry observers note that some of Tacchi, Jr.’s ashes were also packed away inside four .50-caliber shells that will now remain aboard the B-25. According to Jenner, their departed colleague will “fly with us forever,” thanks to his final request.

“[He] had such a deep interest in history, as well as the airplanes, and it was so much a part of his life,” Jenner added. “I think it was natural for him to pick that way to say goodbye.”.

It has been revealed that before it received its nickname, Show Me, the B-25 was simply classified by the United States Air Force as 44-31385. It first took to the sky in January 1945 and was used as a trainer for upcoming pilots. Show me is technically a B-25J—the final variant of the aircraft which also featured an eight-gun strafer nose.

The military retired 44-31385 at Arizona’s Davis Monthan Air Force Base in 1958, before selling it to its first private owner the following year. A windstorm damaged the bomber a decade later while it was stored in Seymour, Illinois. Show Me remained grounded in Seymour until it was finally repaired in 1975. The Commemorative Air Force’s Missouri Wing received the B-25 in 1982.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the BMW iX5 is a big deal for the German automaker.
  • It has been revealed that in other words, the iX5 has a lot on its shoulders, so it has to deliver.
  • The test, which was performed on a closed course, started when the battery still had 4% energy left.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the BMW iX5 is a big deal for the German automaker. It’s the firm’s first electric X5, a model that has traditionally been one of its best-sellers, and it’s also the first electric BMW assembled in the United States.

It has been revealed that in other words, the iX5 has a lot on its shoulders, so it has to deliver. Thankfully, the automaker crammed a massive, 144-kilowatt-hour battery under the SUV’s body, and now a new test from Out of Spec Testing reveals just how much range is hidden in the EV’s pack, even after the instrument cluster indicates there’s nothing more to give.

The test, which was performed on a closed course, started when the battery still had 4% energy left. The car’s displays said that the driver should recharge at the next opportunity, which makes a lot of sense in the real world, but the SUV still drove normally. At 2% state of charge, the car’s brain limited the power output to roughly 350 horsepower, down from approximately 450 hp, but that’s still plenty.

At 1%, the iX5 still delivered plenty of performance, and the driver still managed to maintain speeds between 35 and 55 miles per hour. The same speeds were still possible when the battery level reached zero, but a turtle icon appeared on the dash, accompanied by a yellow power meter and a warning message telling the driver to avoid heavy acceleration and overtaking.

All this being said, the iX5 did not slow down. It soldiered on, covering 8.4 miles after the battery level had reached 0% and consuming almost 3 kWh from the battery that was supposedly empty. The pedal started to feel a little softer at the 10-mile mark, and the first substantial power cut came at 10.7 miles, when the car stopped taking accelerator inputs and started slowing down.

Industry observers note that but that wasn’t the end of the test. The iX5 was restarted and, surprisingly, continued driving at speeds of up to 55 mph. After consuming 7.4 kWh from the reserve, the iX5 eventually shut down, slowing down to a standstill and automatically engaging Park. It drove a total of 21.8 miles after the instrument cluster first showed that the battery had 0% energy left.

A second restart attempt was unsuccessful, but it goes to show that BMW put quite a big buffer on the iX5’s battery. It also means that the SUV’s total battery capacity is somewhere around 151 kWh.

It has been revealed that range-wise, the 2027 BMW iX5 60 xDrive, the only version right now available, can drive up to 456 miles on a full battery, according to the EPA. In a recent comparison with the Lucid Gravity, Porsche Cayenne, and Rivian R1S, the iX5 covered 411 miles at 70 mph, beating all of its competitors by at least 43 miles.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that one of the most common questions asked by first-time EV buyers is about the cost of electricity. Whether they plan to charge at home or find charging in the wild, everyone wants to know what to expect when it comes time to top off their batteries. One EV owner did the math after two months of EV ownership and came up with a surprising number: $7 a month.

Recent findings suggest that whether we’re talking gasoline, diesel, or electricity, one driver’s fuel costs can look dramatically different from another’s. How far they drive, how often, and under what conditions can matter just as much as what they drive. And while EVs may offer the greatest benefits to rural drivers covering long distances, a Redditor going by Suitable-Truth-350 took a different approach, moving into a highly walkable city for the express purpose of driving as little as possible.

According to recent reports, “My wife and I recently retired and moved from a car dependent, rural/suburban area to a large, walkable city with good light rail. Our goal was to drive as little as possible,” write Suitable-Truth-350. “We took delivery of an Ioniq5 in August. We still have a daily walking life, but we use the car to see friends in the country, shop or travel around the greater Chicagoland area. After 2 months, we finally charged it.”.

It has been revealed that the result? Suitable says it took less than 30 minutes to juice their Ioniq 5 back up to an 80% SOC, at a total cost of $13.

“Driving the car is a pleasure,” they continue. “The pickup and smooth operation so different from our last ICE vehicle. First impression, we love the car and could never imagine going back to (a gasoline-powered car).”.

Industry observers note that I’ve been saying it for years: drive an EV for a week and whatever range anxiety you might experience will disappear. And, while it seems like Suitable-Truth-350 didn’t have much range anxiety to begin with, it’s worth noting here that their situation isn’t that rare.

In their most recent national survey, AAA found that the average US driver covered less than 29 miles per day, with the vast majority weekly commuting totals falling well within the range of even the most affordable used EVs.

The same survey found that just 30% of Americans reported taking at least one road trip the previous summer, with an average one-way trip length of ~235 miles.

That 235 mile trip might be too much for a car like the Fiat 500e, but even that car – the new EV with the shortest EPA-estimated range you can buy in the US – can make a 235 mile trip with a single 30-minute stop to charge. And in 2026 and 2027, they’re sure to find plenty of places to charge, thanks to a public charging network that’s newer, faster, and far more built out than they probably think, with more fast-charging locations opening every week and modern charging speeds that make longer stops the exception instead of the norm.

Our two EVs raised our monthly electric bill by ~ $60/mo. and that's without solar. That wouldn't have paid for one gas fill-up for a week in our previous gas cars. I don't think this is even a question. If you can charge at home, it's cheaper. If you rely on public charging all the time then it's a mixed bag but still generally cheaper in most parts of the country. All remarked, we have three EVs now and my monthly electric bill for our entire house with six people is less than what we paid for fuel in one gas car.

In other words: your charging costs are probably going to be higher than Suitable-Truth-350’s seven-ish dollars per month, but with $4/gallon premium and $6/gallon diesel still very much the norm in 2026, it’ll probably be less than you think, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it looks to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a substantial component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the new maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios claims the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

In a recent development, the blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of big maps as Battlefield 6 right now is.

Industry observers note that another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. Interestingly, there appears to be some sort of mechanic unique to Contaminated that the developer also wants to evaluate.

In a recent development, more Labs sessions are planned, including one that will show off new gameplay tools and vehicles. The AH-6 Little Bird helicopter was specifically namedropped, which makes sense given that it’s going to be part of Season 2’s content.

Sources indicate that battlefield Labs sessions will also extend beyond the biggest-ticket items of maps and vehicles. BF Studios said we should expect tests of upcoming features, like the Aircraft Radar, as part of a list of other air combat updates.

Industry observers note that ground vehicles, and they way the various rockets interact with them, will also be evaluated in a different session, with specific adjustments planned for RPGs and TOWs. And, of course, the work to improve and perfect hit reg remains ongoing, and future tweaks will go through Labs first.

Sources indicate that there’s even more exciting news for fans of big maps, as the blog post also confirmed that Battlefield 4’s Golmud Railway is currently in the works, planned to go live in a future season. Golmud Railway will show up early in Labs, and you can expect it to evolve over multiple sessions.

It has been revealed that for context, when it does arrive in Battlefield 6, Golmud Railway will be the largest map in the game, which is saying something. Though the map is beloved by vehicle players, it has its challenges elsewhere, and BF Studios states it will be looking at all that when it creates the BF6, emphasising that it won’t be a simple port of the BF4 original.

Finally, the post throws a bone to Redsec battle royale players still waiting for a Solo mode. BF Studios continues to test the idea internally, but it’s taking a while. Needless to say, there are so many aspects that need to be considered. Game pace, balance, player survivability, match flow just to name a few.

In a recent development, redsec BR was built with squads in mind, so that task is extra challenging. Though the developer didn’t say when we can expect Solos to arrive in Labs, players will get a chance to experience it before it enters the live game.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peel the name tags off the Mazda Cosmo, and it could easily pass for an American car.
  • Industry observers note that the Cosmo is something of a mystery car.
  • In a recent development, that’s the situation in the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From the April 1977 glitch of Car and Driver.

Peel the name tags off the Mazda Cosmo, and it could easily pass for an American car. The two-rotor Wankel is as smooth and vibra­tionless as any V-8, the car is easily as quiet inside as a typical intermediate sedan, and the Cosmo’s body even has the same sort of creaky flexibility that we’ve come to expect of Detroit cars. If we didn’t know better, we might think this was a upcoming subcompact Buick or perhaps a miniature Camaro. Never would we confuse it with a Toyota or Datsun.

Industry observers note that the Cosmo is something of a mystery car. It was designed with the United States in mind—a fast, smooth sports coupe for a country that swallowed Datsun Z-cars as fast as the ships could unload them at the ports. But for some reason, the Cosmo never struck the American fancy. Maybe it was the bad publicity heaped on the rotary engine; per­haps the dull colors and unfortunate combi­nation of mag wheels and white-wall tires turned off the sporty-car buyer. And we can’t entirely disregard the thought that a coupe with a Vega silhouette, Oldsmobile waterfall grille, and Plymouth Cricket taillights may sim­ply be the wrong thing to wave in American faces. But whatever the reason, Cosmos tend to languish in the showrooms.

See all results for used cars for sale near 98531.

In a recent development, that’s the situation in the U.S. In Japan, the Cosmo is last season’s smash hit, named Car of the Year by one of the country’s auto mag­azines and the next best thing in Tokyo to driving a foreign car. (The Japanese, like many Americans, tend to think that anything imported is probably better and certainly more fun than the made-at-home equivalent). The car looks great in its own neighborhood. It has slightly different—but not much small­er—bumpers and the mandatory mirrors perched out on the front fenders halfway to the headlights. But apart from those two de­tails, the Japanese-market Cosmo looks the same as the one we tend to ignore here.

We humbly submit, at this point, that the Cosmo deserves another look, if for no other reason than it features one commodity in de­cidedly short supply elsewhere—horsepower. This car is quick. The engine is wide awake above 2000 rpm, and it climbs to 7000 with­out a backward glance. Freeways abound with legions of 350 four-barrels that won’t match the Cosmo’s pace. And as amazing as it may seem, none of them can come close to the Mazda’s gas mileage. The 1977 model with the standard five-speed trans­mission has been weaned down to 32 mpg highway and 20 mpg city for a combined rating of 25 mpg in the EPA mileage sweep­stakes. That is excellent economy for a car of this performance level.

Industry observers note that while the Cosmo is surprisingly economical, it is by no means austere. The interior offers about the same amount of useful space for four occupants as a Camaro, and the trunk, because it stows its spare more ef­ficiently than the Chevrolet, is at least as good. Yet overall, the Mazda Cosmo is about the same size as a Corvette, actually slightly smaller.

See all results for used cars for sale near 98531.

The quality of the interior is also on par with that of Detroit models. The dash is molded vinyl with a minimum of seams, and indicates the driver a full complement of instruments set in a field of imitation wood. Velour cloth covers the seats and door panels. There is even a trapezoid opera window to delight the double-knit crowd. And if that doesn’t knock them dead at the Donut Center, show them the wire-spoked steering wheel.

In a recent development, there is just one aspect of the Mazda’s er­satz Detroit personality with which we take is­sue: It’s a smooth-road car. On ribbons of un­broken concrete the Cosmo simply glides along, but when the going gets rough, so does the ride. The front wheels steer notice­ably over bumps, and the suspension travel is limited enough so that the wheels are occa­sionally jerked clear of the road on surfaces that are not really that rough. The balance of the car, particularly on smooth roads, is rea­sonable however.

It has been revealed that at least the Cosmo’s ailments are the kind that can be fixed, certainly by a second look at the factory and perhaps even with a few bolt-on aftermarket parts. We would start with the shocks and see what happens. The rotary engine, on the other hand, is just fine as it is. And Mazda provides an incredible warranty—­five years or 75,000 miles—to make sure it stays that way. Nobody can dislike a car that is guaranteed to keep running even after the loan is paid off.

Honda Recalling Thousands of S2000s for Potential Fuel Leak

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (292 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it’s not too often we get fresh recalls for older cars like the Honda S2000, but today is one of those days.
  • According to recent reports, the reason for the recall is that the “fuel flange joint assembly may have been improperly manufactured.” As a consequence, Honda states this could allow the fuel line connection to loosen and separate, ultimately resulting in a fuel leak and engine stall.
  • Honda notes that when part production shifted locations, 67 replacement parts were produced without brazing material.

Sources indicate that it’s not too often we get fresh recalls for older cars like the Honda S2000, but today is one of those days. According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, Honda is recalling 16,387 S2000 roadsters from the 2004–20005 model years, the first two years of the AP2 refresh. A quick look at the sales figures for those years seems to suggest that means all (or close to all) S2000s from those years are part of the recall population.

According to recent reports, the reason for the recall is that the “fuel flange joint assembly may have been improperly manufactured.” As a consequence, Honda states this could allow the fuel line connection to loosen and separate, ultimately resulting in a fuel leak and engine stall. The problem with manufacturing relates to whether or not it was built with brazing material at the joint-to-flange connection. With the part being a push-to-fit part, Honda says this lack of material could cause the connection to become loose and separate.

Honda notes that when part production shifted locations, 67 replacement parts were produced without brazing material. These parts were shipped and potentially installed in S2000s. Honda estimates the percentage of cars with the defect is 1 percent. There won’t be many warning signs before it’s too late to continue driving, but Honda says stalling, a misfire, fuel odor and an inability to start the engine are all symptoms.

As of now, Honda says there are no injuries or deaths related to this matter. Those with cars in the recall range will have to bring their convertibles into the Honda dealer for the remedy. Once there, it will receive a new and improved fuel flange joint assembly free of charge.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

China’s SC01 electric sports car, which wowed reviewers for its great handling and back-to-basics approach to EVs, is getting its own European factory, with a scheduled production start in May 2027.

Recent findings suggest that the two-door EV, which was developed by Tianjin Gongjiangpai Auto Technology (TGAT), will be assembled at a fresh facility in central Italy by FIPA Europe, a company that currently makes Chinese microcars. The importer has signed a contract for an existing industrial complex in the Marche region, and work is expected to begin early next year, according to Electrive.

The first phase of the European SC01 program involves a 20,000-square-meter (21,527-square-feet) production space and 50 employees who will work to assemble the electric two-seater from kits shipped from China. A 2,750-square-meter (29,600 sq ft) warehouse and a 20,000-square-meter (21,5278 sq ft) logistics area are also planned for the upcoming facility.

However, that’s just the start, as FIPA Europe intends to expand the floor space and its headcount by the end of the decade, with 285 jobs expected by the last day of 2030. The manufacturer, which assembles the Desner T80, a low-speed electric microcar, claims to be the only authorized importer and manufacturer of the SC01 for the European Union and the only company responsible for the car’s European homologation.

Industry observers note that the first SC01 prototypes are reportedly already roaming Italy’s streets, imported from China for development purposes. The next step is to install the assembly lines at the new factory in the first quarter of 2027, with the first Italian-built SC01s scheduled to roll out the door in May.

As a reminder, the Chinese-spec SC01 is powered by a 430-horsepower (320-kilowatt) dual-motor powertrain that draws electricity from a 60-kilowatt-hour battery pack. The car was developed with backing from tech giant Xiaomi and is assembled in China by JMEV, a joint venture between Groupe Renault and Jiangling Motors Corporation Group.

It has been revealed that the car’s biggest trait is its low weight. Tipping the scales at less than 1,400 kilograms (3,086 pounds), it’s lighter than a Porsche 911 and can sprint from zero to 62 mph (0-100 kilometers per hour) in 2.9 seconds. What’s more, the car’s dual-motor powertrain can be configured to work either independently or together, so the driver can choose from rear-wheel drive, front-wheel drive, or all-wheel drive.

According to recent reports, inside, there’s just the bare minimum, with a digital instrument cluster and a few physical controls on the center console. There’s no infotainment screen, let alone a passenger display, as is the case with many modern luxury cars nowadays.

Pricing hasn’t been revealed for the European version of the SC01, but in China, the back-to-basics EV retails for the equivalent of about $32,000.

Tech Report: Trash-hungry robots roam Japan’s busiest train station

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (590 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A jingle-playing, googly-eyed team of trash-collecting robots are vying to make the world’s busiest rail station a bit cleaner.
  • Sources indicate that east Japan Railway Company (referred to as JR East), which runs several lines in Tokyo’s bustling Shinjuku Station, recently wrapped up a roughly 10-week trial of these eye-catching robots.
  • Each of the three robots sports a different color (green, yellow, or red) to match their accompanying rail line.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A jingle-playing, googly-eyed team of trash-collecting robots are vying to make the world’s busiest rail station a bit cleaner.

Sources indicate that east Japan Railway Company (referred to as JR East), which runs several lines in Tokyo’s bustling Shinjuku Station, recently wrapped up a roughly 10-week trial of these eye-catching robots. The machines stand just over three feet tall, and roll autonomously along preprogrammed routes through the station’s underground concourses between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m. Once full, they trundle back to the station’s garbage collection area on their own.

Each of the three robots sports a different color (green, yellow, or red) to match their accompanying rail line. They definitely don’t look like your average sad, overflowing waste bin. Instead, they stroll up to commuters with bright lights and a front-facing screen showing cartoon eyes. Music appears to play when trash gets fed into them. An accompanying illustration of  Shinjukuma, the station’s bear mascot, reveals passengers which bins are for general trash and which are for plastic bottles. It’s all very Japanese.

JR East officials are hoping these bins on wheels will help relieve some of the burden on garbage collectors who struggle to keep up with trash generated by the millions  of people  passing through every day. The station, which sits on the western edge of central Tokyo, sees nearly three million daily passengers, an absurd amount of foot traffic that earned it a Guinness World Record. But more people means more trash. According to Tokyo Weekender, sanitation workers in the station unload garbage from fixed bags more than 10 times per day.

Sources indicate that the robots could help, but only if they don’t get in the way and create more problems than they solve. Though JR East reportedly tested out a pair of garbage robots back in 2023, that was in a much smaller station and only for three days. Shinjuku is a much bigger challenge and serves as a kind of stress test to see if they are able to operate safely and effectively in densely packed areas.

Tokyo isn’t the only city experimenting with trash robots. A cat-themed, mobile trash unit made a brief appearance in Paris’ Charles De Gaulle airport last year. In Singapore, an autonomous robot started collecting garbage in 2019 at Jewel Changi Airport, the shopping complex attached to the city’s main airport. And while trash collection is still relatively niche, automated cleaning robots are rapidly becoming mainstays in many modern transportation hubs. Houston, Baltimore, Pittsburgh, and Oakland are among the many  cities in the United States already putting robot cleaners to work scrubbing and mopping airport floors.

Making these robots seem cute isn’t just for attracting selfies. It’s also a self-defense strategy. Humans have a mixed track record when it comes to sharing space with robots. In 2024, the Upcoming York Police Department retired a 400-pound, egg-shaped surveillance robot from patrolling subway lines after facing pushback from privacy activists and concerned citizens, some of whom felt uncomfortable near the lifeless, imposing monitor. Years earlier, a friendly hitchhiking robot called HitchBot made it about two weeks into its trip across the United States when it was found vandalized and beheaded in Philadelphia.

Sources indicate that could cartoon eyes and a cute mascot have saved those robots? It’s difficult to say, but at least the Tokyo garbage robots seemed to make it through their trial without any dissected parts. That’s an improvement.

#166720. Tesla introduces FSD v15, targets its biggest weaknesses, from signs to potholes

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1300 w)

Tesla introduces FSD v15, targets its biggest weaknesses, from signs to potholes

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1300 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla has started rolling out “Full Self-Driving” v15, and its list of improvements reads like a list of FSD’s biggest current weaknesses: sign detection, potholes, and speed handling in school zones.
  • Sources indicate that tesla also claims “25x better handling of safety critical cases” and is adding a new live visualization that looks seriously impressive.
  • Tesla revealed the rollout on X this afternoon, and its Tesla Super Intelligence account followed up with the full release notes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has started rolling out “Full Self-Driving” v15, and its list of improvements reads like a list of FSD’s biggest current weaknesses: sign detection, potholes, and speed handling in school zones.

Sources indicate that tesla also claims “25x better handling of safety critical cases” and is adding a new live visualization that looks seriously impressive. If the driving improvements are as real as the visuals, this is a significant patch.

Tesla revealed the rollout on X this afternoon, and its Tesla Super Intelligence account followed up with the full release notes. The organization didn’t say which vehicles get it first, but it has previously told investors that its AI4 (HW4) computer is enough to run v15.

Here are Tesla’s release notes for FSD v15:.

According to recent reports, v15 upgrades every part of the end-to-end driving network. Includes:.

Tesla’s main announcement also says FSD can now slow down for speed cameras, and it adds Bike Rack Mode, which allows FSD with a bike rack or a similar hitch accessory. Navigation learning only covers the start and end of trips for now; Tesla says later v15 releases will expand it to the entire route.

In a recent development, the fresh visualization is the flashiest part, and based on the video Tesla shared, it’s super impressive. The center screen demonstrates a detailed, rendered version of the street around the car, far beyond the current FSD visualization.

FSD v15 now starting to roll out – upgrading every part of the end-to-end driving network Safety25x better handling of safety critical casesTesla Reality View Adds a live visualization of the drive that lets you see & control what FSD is planning to doNavigation for start… pic.twitter.com/Sfjk4wZecW.

Tesla calls it “Reality View” in its announcement and “Tesla Augmented Reality” in the release notes. The notes say it replaces all the separate model signals with a single end-to-end visualization that uses less compute, and Tesla states it lets the driver “see & control what FSD is planning to do.” If that works as advertised, it could make supervising the system a lot easier.

What stands out more is where Tesla is focusing. Almost every driving improvement in the release notes targets an area where FSD struggles today.

Signs are a big one. In a test published in September, Brussels nonprofit Johanna.be found that FSD exceeded the limit in 55% of the 30 km/h zones it drove through, averaging 44 km/h. In most of those zones, the car’s screen revealed a 50 km/h limit. It didn’t read the sign.

Recent findings suggest that potholes are another. In August, Musk said pothole avoidance was “coming soon”, something he had already promised back in 2019. Today, FSD still drives straight through them.

Industry observers note that school zones are on the list too. NHTSA is reviewing a petition claiming Tesla’s Robotaxis speed through active school zones, on top of an investigation it opened in October 2025 into FSD traffic-law violations like running red lights. Slowing for speed cameras fits the same theme, though it also suggests Tesla is fine with FSD going over the limit when there’s no camera around.

So if v15 really fixes these, it’s a very good upgrade. The question is by how much.

In a recent development, one change goes the other way. Tesla says it is “decreasing strictness” of driver monitoring in higher-speed driver profiles, at a time when sleeping drivers on FSD keep making headlines and Tesla is tightening monitoring in Europe at regulators’ request.

According to recent reports, the release notes clear up what the “25x” refers to: Tesla indicates the new vision encoder improves the critical intervention rate by 25x. That’s the right metric to measure progress toward unsupervised driving. But Tesla still doesn’t share the actual number, only the multiplier.

The math gets interesting fast. Our data from earlier this year suggested FSD v14 could go a couple thousand miles between critical interventions. A 25x improvement on that would put v15 around 50,000 miles between critical interventions, well beyond the roughly 10,000 miles we’ve noted Tesla needs for a limited unsupervised service. If that were true across the fleet, we could see Tesla having its most meaningful push toward autonomy in a long time.

In a recent development, and v15 already carries plenty of hype. In April, Elon Musk wrote that v15 “will far exceed human levels of safety, even in completely unsupervised and complex situations.” We pointed out at the time that he had said similar things about v12 and v14. In August, Tesla told JPMorgan that v15 is a “step-change” built on seven “core technologies,” with about 40% of them already running in its Robotaxi fleet in Austin.

According to recent reports, FSD has never improved in a straight line. Every major version has brought real gains along with new problems, and point releases regularly go backward.

When v14 arrived in October 2025, it came with hallucinations, brake stabbing, and excessive speeding, and early crowdsourced data highlighted about 732 miles between critical disengagements, below what we expected. It then improved a lot. Then the v14.2 updates went backward before Musk sold v14.3 as the version where “the last massive piece of the puzzle finally lands.”.

Seven months and a long string of point releases later, owners are still supervising, and Tesla now needs v15 to deliver what v14.3 was supposed to.

I was in Austin this week the Cybercabs are everywhere and I used them to get around, the app let you choose model Y or Cybercab. I can't believe they are operational and how many there are along with all the other self driving cars in the city. Experience was excellent. Only issue was they were not able to goto to and from the airport for some reason.

Recent findings suggest that the visuals are super impressive. That much we can already judge from the video, and Reality View could make FSD easier to understand and supervise.

The driving side is harder to judge. Tesla is going straight at the weaknesses that owners and regulators complain about most: misread speed limits, potholes, school zones, debris. If v15 delivers real progress on all of those, it’s a really good patch.

Sources indicate that but “improved detection” doesn’t tell us how much better, and a 25x multiplier without the underlying number is hard to check. FSD has gone two steps forward, one step back throughout its history, with point releases regularly breaking things the previous version handled fine. And Tesla still won’t publish the disengagement data that would settle it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that when people spend nearly $2 million on a two-seat, mid-engine car, you can safely assume it is not the only car in their garage.
  • But Spyker CEO Victor Muller has a different idea.
  • It has been revealed that that's a refreshing philosophy from someone selling a car this pricey.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that when people spend nearly $2 million on a two-seat, mid-engine car, you can safely assume it is not the only car in their garage. It makes sense that it will not be driven every day; however, often times cars like this are not really driven at all. They spend their entire lives in climate-controlled garages, tucked beneath soft covers. And when the car in question is something like a one-of-25 C8 Preliator XXV Coupé, the temptation to preserve it as a collectible is understandable.

But Spyker CEO Victor Muller has a different idea. He wants his customers to get behind the wheel and drive. "We prefer to sell our cars to people that actually use them," Muller told me during an interview at Retromobile New York. "Because that's what I made them for. To drive the hell out of them.".

It has been revealed that that's a refreshing philosophy from someone selling a car this pricey. Particularly when that car is the upcoming C8 Preliator XXV Coupé, which looks as much like a piece of fine jewelry as an 800-horsepower road rocket. Unfortunately, Muller admits that many of Spyker's previous creations haven't enjoyed particularly active lives.

"Many of our cars, of the 252 we made so far, have just ended up in dungeons, in vaults, in spaces where nobody will ever see them," Muller said. He's hoping to change that by organizing more owner events and encouraging customers to spend time enjoying their cars; Spyker has joined the Supercar Owners Circle, a global network of car collectors, and is planning gatherings in Europe and the United States.

The manufacturer is also in a position where it can be selective about who gets its cars. According to Muller, all 25 Preliator XXV Coupés sold during their debut at The Quail, a Motorsports Gathering in August. Every single one was snapped up in a day. "I've never seen anything like that in my entire life," he remarked. Spyker plans to build 25 Spyders and 25 Sedancas in 2028, he added, once production of the Coupés is complete next year.

Who is buying these cars has changed dramatically over the last quarter century. "In 2000, my typical customer was a fifty-five to sixty-year-old industrialist—old money, car collector, very astute buyer," Muller explained. "Fast forward twenty five years. Your average age is thirty-five years. Tech investor. Huge collection. Knows his cars completely. But nobody asks how much it is.".

According to recent reports, muller states approximately 40 percent of his new buyers are existing or former Spyker owners, and roughly 80 percent of the new cars are expected to go to the United States. But no matter how old the buyer is or where they live, Muller wants them to drive the cars. This makes sense when you understand his approach to engineering; The new car has no massive infotainment screens or hybrid systems, and electronic intervention is largely limited to essential safety features like ABS and stability control.

“If you mis-shift in a Spyker and you drive two hundred miles an hour and you shift to second gear, you blow up the engine," Muller noted. "And I think it has to be that way in Spyker world." For Spyker, the connection between driver and machine is more important than chasing lap records, acceleration figures and electronic nannies. "If you don't like that, buy something else," he added. "If not, man up—drive a Spyker.".

Another way to demonstrate that these cars are meant to be driven is to get the brand back into racing. Muller revealed that Spyker is taking steps toward returning to professional endurance competition. The tech giant competed in the 24 Hours of Le Mans eight times, most recently in 2010. Naturally, I asked whether another trip to Le Mans might be in Spyker's future.

It has been revealed that "Absolutely," Muller said. "We'd love to go back in racing." Muller says Spyker is preparing to re-enter endurance racing, although he stopped short of announcing a timeline, championship, or confirmed race entry. He certainly likes the idea of seeing his latest creation on the track. More importantly, he's already started putting people in place to make it happen.

"I actually hired my former GT2 race director again," Muller said. "He started a week ago today.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it’s no secret that electric cars are more affordable to maintain than their gasoline-powered counterparts. While they may have a higher purchase price than a comparable gas-powered vehicle, EVs can save owners money over time by eliminating the need for regular engine oil changes, emissions tests, and other traditional maintenance tasks. Affordable electric vehicles are also becoming increasingly common, with even more options expected to arrive in the coming years.

According to recent reports, however, that doesn't mean electric cars are completely maintenance-free. Like any other vehicle, EVs require regular care and attention to remain reliable and perform at their best for many years.

Although they don't have conventional combustion engines or traditional automatic transmissions, electric cars still feature components that require periodic maintenance. These include reduction gearboxes, brake fluid, brake pads, coolant systems, and tires among other things. Keeping these components in good condition is essential to ensuring an EV's long-term reliability.

ERANGE EV tires are purpose-built for electric vehicles, combining efficiency, comfort and performance with advanced EcoPoint3 technology.

In a recent development, for the second installment of our EV maintenance series, I'll be taking a closer look at the Hyundai Ioniq 5, one of the most recognizable electric crossovers on the market. Made in the United States and South Korea, the Ioniq 5 has long been one of the biggest rivals to the ubiquitous Tesla Model Y.

I'll break down Hyundai's recommended maintenance schedule, explaining which items are required to keep the vehicle running smoothly over the long term.

Sources indicate that compared to Tesla, which is known for its rather skimpy maintenance plan, Hyundai includes a generous list of maintenance items in the owner’s manual. The automaker also includes additional service actions that should be performed if the car is used in harsher-than-normal conditions, so owners know what to expect in the long run.

It has been revealed that there’s a normal maintenance schedule and a separate section for severe usage and low mileage conditions. Hyundai also has a list of maintenance items that can be performed by the owner. I’ll go through all of them, so drivers can easily mark down what needs to be done during the car’s lifetime.

According to recent reports, hyundai says that normal driving conditions include distances longer than 10 miles, clean roads without salt or dust, ambient temperatures under 90ºF (32ºC), no towing, no roof rack, and normal speeds. Under these conditions, the required maintenance for a Hyundai Ioniq 5 is as follows, according to the owner’s manual:.

It has been revealed that according to Hyundai, extra precaution needs to be taken if the car is driven under certain conditions. These include repeated driving short distances of less than five miles in normal temperatures or less than 10 miles in freezing temperatures, and driving on rough, dusty, muddy, unpaved, graveled, or salt-spread roads.

It has been revealed that but that’s not all. Driving in areas using salt or other corrosive materials, or in very cold weather, driving in heavy dust conditions, driving in heavy traffic areas with the ambient temperature higher than 90ºF (32 ºC) while consuming more than 50% of electric energy, and driving on uphill, downhill, or mountain roads repeatedly can also result in extra maintenance items.

Towing a trailer, using a roof rack, driving as a patrol car or taxi, frequently driving at high speeds, and frequently driving in stop-and-go conditions are also part of the conditions that lead to more intense servicing requirements.

In addition to the normal maintenance schedule above, Hyundai recommends the following actions for severe usage and low-mileage conditions:.

All of these items should be performed by a Hyundai technician, but the Ioniq 5 also has a consistent list of maintenance actions that should be performed by the owner.

The Hyundai Ioniq 5 is one of the best-selling electric crossovers in the United States, and for good reason. Its unique styling has plenty of fans, and it’s a genuinely nice car to drive. As for its maintenance requirements, the official recommendations have a lot more items compared to the Tesla Model Y, but at the end of the day, most of them are just inspection jobs. As a result, maintenance costs should be quite low compared to a comparable gas vehicle. Just rotate and replace tires, keep an eye on your brakes, and swap out the coolant after 10 years or 120,000 miles.

Here are 7 great reasons rural drivers SHOULD embrace EVs in 2027

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1701 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that america’s heartland is full of rural communities that are miles away from its major cities, both geographically and culturally – but that doesn’t mean these more sparsely populated regions can’t reap the benefits of electrification.
  • UPDATE 21NOV2026: this is an annual (ish) post I have been updating since 2024.
  • Sources indicate that “An electric lifestyle would be a boon to our rural heartland,” wrote the Union of Concerned Scientists’ Maria Cecilia Pinto de Moura.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that america’s heartland is full of rural communities that are miles away from its major cities, both geographically and culturally – but that doesn’t mean these more sparsely populated regions can’t reap the benefits of electrification. In fact, EVs offer rural drivers even more benefits than they do to city-dwellers!

UPDATE 21NOV2026: this is an annual (ish) post I have been updating since 2024.

Sources indicate that “An electric lifestyle would be a boon to our rural heartland,” wrote the Union of Concerned Scientists’ Maria Cecilia Pinto de Moura. “Rural communities across the country have their own distinguishing characteristics, but certain shared characteristics such as driving distances, the type of vehicles driven, and socio-economics are factors which contribute to this larger potential to benefit from vehicle electrification.”.

Pinto de Moura went on to outline five ways rural and country drivers could benefit from going electric – but that was in 2021, and a whole lot has changed in the nearly six years since. As such, I thought it was high time we revisit some of the reasons EVs are a great fit for rural lifestyles, see if we could uncover any new ones, and outline the reasons we think rural drivers should rush to embrace electric vehicles in the coming calendar year.

According to recent reports, when you hear that line about, “the average American drives 30 to 40 miles a day,” remember that in towns like Wellington, Ohio, or Colfax, Washington, 30 miles is a grocery run. Each way. So when people trot out that old line about range anxiety, what rural drivers actually hear isn’t reassurance. It’s dismissal — a suggestion that they drive too far for an EV to work, when nothing could be further from the truth.

A recent study by Rural Climate Partnership found that rural drivers spend an average of 44% more on fuel than city dwellers, and that the top 3.6% of rural drivers — the “supermilers” who rack up the most miles — could save over $4,000 each year by switching to electric fuel.

Country guys and gals love their pickups, and arguably the biggest difference between the EV market of 2021 and 2027 is that electric trucks and SUVs are no longer a novelty. There are now battery-powered options ready to haul, handle chores, head out camping, and tow a trailer.

What’s more, a newly introduced wave of more affordable electric trucks from Ford, Slate, and others is challenging the idea that you need a $50,000 half-ton pickup to get real work done. Early interest suggests there’s plenty of pent-up demand for capable, accessible electric work trucks that don’t need to be twenty feet long or cost more than what your parent’s paid for their house.

Sources indicate that with only about 45% of rural counties having access to DC fast charging, public charging still isn’t as visible as many first-time EV buyers might like, but it’s far better than it used to be — and improving fast. Still, that’s not the real EV advantage. Home charging is.

Recent findings suggest that unlike many apartment-dwelling urban drivers, most rural owners can charge right at home. More than 80% of rural households have a driveway or garage that are ideal for overnight Level 2 charging, and many already have a 240V outlet, keeping setup costs (if there even are any) to a minimum.

Plug in before bed, wake up to a full battery every morning, and do it for pennies on the dollar, especially with off-peak rates.

In a recent development, if disaster strikes and you lose power, your EV could be more than just a way to get around. Many electric cars and trucks have the ability to power refrigerators, freezers, well pumps, lights, and other household essentials for days, either through onboard outlets or a dedicated vehicle-to-home (V2H) system that feeds electricity directly into your home’s electrical panel. Ford’s from-the-ashes F-150 Lightning and Tesla’s Cybertruck are already among the EVs making that capability a reality, and newer, more affordable electric trucks promise to bring V2H tech to even more households.

If you live in an area prone to extreme weather, where severe storms, hurricanes, or wildfires can leave homes without electricity for days, that’s a pretty compelling benefit. Keeping food cold, medical equipment running or essential medication refrigerated can be a literal lifesaver – and your EV’s battery might be the biggest backup power source you own.

Sources indicate that it’s been a few years since a working class guy could reasonably expect to get a new pickup for less than $50,000. And, while much has been made of the “high cost of electric vehicles,” the truth is that thanks to killer lease deals, new tax incentives, and companies like Ford Pro and TRC that are willing to help you find even more funding to help pay for them, EVs can often be had for less than a comparable gas model.

As such, getting behind the wheel of an ultra-powerful, ultra smooth-running electric pickup truck from your favorite brand is easier than ever.

At the risk of sounding like a paranoid red hat, rural Americans are proud Americans – just like rural Canadians are proud Canadians. Unfortunately, every gallon of gas burned in their pickups and SUVs came from oil drilled, refined, and traded on global markets — and that means supporting the oil business and economies of nations whose values don’t always align with, or maybe are even outright hostile to theirs.

Switching to an EV can help more of that money right here at home, especially as more and better battery recycling efforts come online and newer battery and anode/cathode chemistries are developed, reducing dependence on rare Earth metals, cobalt, and even lithium.

Even better, thanks to the rapid expansion and dramatically reduced costs of wind and solar power, you can power your EV with energy that is 100% Made in the USA, that doesn’t support foreign oil interests or involve you in a bunch of dumb oil wars (except indirectly), and which creates good-paying construction and maintenance jobs for local workers.

In my experience, rural buyers appreciate things that last, and are moved more by lasting quality than fleeting fashions – and that’s exactly why they should be looking at EVs.

We recently covered a 2019 Chevy Bolt that had put more than 470,000 miles on its odometer, along with data from Ford showing its battery packs maintain more than 90% of their battery health after 100,000 miles.

According to recent reports, and while we’re talking about data, it should be noted that EVs aren’t some upcoming, unknown technology. The first modern high-voltage car battery hit the road more than 30 years ago (the Prius was released in 1996, as a 1997 model). Some of those cars are still on the road – and there are literally tens of thousands of EVs out there still performing their daily driver duties every day.

There are obviously more reasons to go electric than these, from lower cost of ownership to saving the planet to absolutely killer burnouts that would make the one-tire-fire era IROC Camaros hang their 305s in shame – but I think those kind of fade into the background as being appealing to just about everyone, instead of being especially appealing to rural drivers.

Industry observers note that I live in rural Australia in a village that doesn't even have a fuel bowser. My shopping trip is usually around 164km (100miles). I have solar on my roof. I now have an EV (one of the Chinese brands that aren't available in the USA) and am delighted with it. I'm saving a lot of money on fuel and because the solar feed-in tariff goes negative in the middle of the day (I have to pay the utility company to take my electricity) by charging the car at home I save money there. For rural people with roof space for solar EVs should be a no-brainer, but like many rural areas my district is incredibly conservative (do a search for Barnaby Joyce, my local member) and the populace are convinced they don't drive far enough, they'll catch on fire (mine has an LFP battery, so the risk is low) and that I'll need to replace the battery in a year (even though the battery has an 8 year warranty).

That stated, it’s been a long time since I was back in Ohio, so maybe I’ve forgotten what it’s like. You guys are smart, head on down to the comments and let me know what I missed!

This came in response to X user David Marcus, who noted: "Can't wait for Tesla to offer an embedded Starlink option on all models (beyond the Cybercab).".

Tesla CEO Elon Musk responded directly.

According to recent reports, "Hopefully available toward the end of next year," he remarked in the X reply. "This will be notable for unsupervised FSD, so passengers have high bandwidth everywhere for work and entertainment.".

All of the Cybercabs that recently launched in Dallas have Starlink antennas, Sawyer Merritt on X claims. However, that would require redesigning the roof panels of all existing Tesla models, which isn't exactly easy. Unless owners would be cool with an additional panel being mounted on top of the car, like the major flat antennae we saw being tested on the Cybertruck recently.

In a recent development, however, according to Tesla's AI lead Ashok Elluswamy, Cybercab passengers right now can't connect to Starlink, as it's only used for fleet management, navigation, and customer service. So adding FSD assistance and passenger entertainment would be a couple of steps up from the robotaxi's capabilities.

Teslas with FSD are already pretty capable even where internet connection might be shoddy, such as on secluded trails. Especially now that FSD can show you a real time camera feed of your car's surroundings, so it looks like you're playing Grand Theft Auto with you own car in real life.

Recent findings suggest that even with those restrictions, this HiJet would be incredibly useful for ferrying around livestock feed on a farm, or shuttling small deliveries around a busy factory complex, or even getting evil minions around a hollowed-out volcano lair. If it does pass muster for on-road use where you live, these trucks are surprisingly plucky to drive, and would make for the ultimate DIY partner. Plenty of hunters and fishermen also appreciate four-wheel-drive kei trucks for their ability to squeeze down narrow tracks where full-size pickups can't go.

The bed is also surprisingly flexible, with fold-down sides that transform it into a mini-flatbed truck. The payload is stouter than you'd think, rated for 770 pounds, so though it may be tiny, it's still mighty.

That power goes to the rear wheels through a five-speed manual transmission, or you can hit a button and get power to all four corners. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a red wave of Chinese-built electric vehicles breaks over Europe and Canada, Xiaomi is selling its electric cars outside of China for the first time ever – and its starting its push for global growth with the UAE in 2027.

Xiaomi is selling its electrified vehicles to buyers outside of China for first time this week, with the SU7 sedan, YU7 crossover, and Skynomad SUV now listed for sale throughout the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The organization isn’t going it alone, however.

Xiomi is working local distributor Gargash Prime Automotive, rather than operating its own retail network, with Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun confirming that the manufacturer would officially enter Western car markets next year at the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen held 17NOV.

CarNewsChina reports that Gargash Prime Automotive is offering 13 variants across the Xiaomi SU7 sedan, YU7 SUV, and Skynomad extended-range electric SUV lineup, with retail prices starting at 169,900 AED ($~46,200 US) for the SU7 Standard and climbing all the way up to 375,900 AED ($~102,000 US) for the range-topping SU7 Ultra.

Not to lump a bunch of nations with their own rich heritage and car culture together, but it’s fair to say that drivers in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait love their supercars – and the brand’s Xiaomi SU7 Ultra might be one of the most super of them all, thanks to fully 1,548 hp from three high-torque electric motors, the SU7 Ultra can sprint from 0-100 km/h (62 mph) in under two seconds on its way to a towering, 217 mph top speed.

In a recent development, it’s not just a straight-line speed machine, either. Xiaomi gave its go-fast flagship a serious track-focused makeover on its way to becomig the “Utlra,” complete with carbon-ceramic brakes, an aggressive (if controversial) composite aero package, an enormous rear wing, and a chassis tuned to tackle the turns the Green Hell of the Nürburgring.

And, at a relatively reasonable $102,000 equivalent price, I’d be willing to bet that a lot of the hypercar-loving Emiratis will be eager to get their hands on one.

The first customer deliveries of the Xiaomi SU7 Standard and Ultra, YU7 Standard, and Skynomad N70 Pro models are scheduled for December of this year, with deliveries of the remaining variants scheduled for February 2027.
